title: Integrating Metabolomics and Histopathology: A Method for Metabolite Recovery from Fixed Tissue Specimens
author: Vučković, Ivan
materials: Methylation of methylene glycol HO−CH2−OH+CH3OH ⇄ HO−CH2−OCH3+H2O

Male C57BL/6J mice were obtained from Jackson Laboratories (Bar Harbor, ME) and housed in the Mayo Clinic animal care facility, accredited by the Association for Assessment and Accreditation of Laboratory Animal Care International (AAALAC). All procedures adhered to National Institutes of Health (NIH) guidelines and were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at Mayo Clinic, Rochester. Mice were anesthetized via intraperitoneal injection of ketamine/xylazine. Following laparotomy, the kidneys were exteriorized in the following sequence: the right kidney was harvested after clamping the renal vessels and immediately freeze-clamped in liquid nitrogen using the standard technique,25 while the left kidney (∼200 mg) was immersed in 500 μL of formalin fixative (4% paraformaldehyde) and maintained in fixative at room temperature for approximately 1 month prior to analysis.

steps.title: Prepare animal and harvest kidneys
steps.instruction: House male C57BL/6J mice, anesthetize with intraperitoneal ketamine/xylazine, perform a laparotomy, exteriorize the kidneys, and harvest the right kidney (≈200 mg) and left kidney (≈200 mg).

steps.title: Freeze‑clamp right kidney immediately
steps.instruction: Clamp the renal vessels of the right kidney and plunge the excised organ into liquid nitrogen using the standard freeze‑clamp technique to halt all metabolic reactions.

steps.title: Fix left kidney in formalin
steps.instruction: Immerse the left kidney in 500 µL of 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) fixative (equivalent to neutral buffered 10 % formalin, ~4 % formaldehyde) and store at room temperature for approximately 1 month. For reference, a fixative‑to‑tissue volume ratio of 2:1 for 48 h at 20–22 °C is sufficient for complete fixation.

steps.title: Grind frozen tissue and perform PCA extraction
steps.instruction: Using a liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled tissue pulverizer, grind the frozen right‑kidney tissue, weigh ~32 mg of the powder, add 320 µL ice‑cold 0.6 M perchloric acid (PCA), vortex 20 s, centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, neutralize the supernatant with 100 µL 2 M KHCO₃, then add 100 µL 0.1 M phosphate buffer and 50 µL 1 mM TSP‑d₄ in D₂O, vortex 20 s, and transfer the mixture to a 5‑mm NMR tube.

substeps.instruction: Grind frozen tissue in liquid nitrogen‑cooled pulverizer.
Neutralize supernatant with 100 µL 2 M KHCO₃.
Add 50 µL 1 mM TSP‑d₄ in D₂O.

steps.title: Prepare fixative supernatant NMR sample
steps.instruction: Collect 400 µL of the fixative solution that was in contact with the left kidney, add 100 µL 0.1 M phosphate buffer and 50 µL 1 mM TSP‑d₄ in D₂O, vortex 20 s, and transfer to a 5‑mm NMR tube.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL 1 mM TSP‑d₄ in D₂O.

steps.title: Prepare formalin reference NMR sample
steps.instruction: Mix 400 µL of 4 % PFA, 100 µL 0.1 M phosphate buffer, and 50 µL 1 mM TSP‑d₄ in D₂O, vortex briefly, and place in a 5‑mm NMR tube.

substeps.instruction: Combine 400 µL 4 % PFA, 100 µL 0.1 M phosphate buffer, and 50 µL 1 mM TSP‑d₄ in D₂O.

steps.title: Acquire high‑resolution 1H NMR spectra
steps.instruction: Load each prepared tube into a Bruker 600 MHz spectrometer equipped with a 5 mm BBI room‑temperature probe and SampleJet changer; maintain sample temperature at 298.2 ± 0.1 K using the BTO 2000 variable‑temperature unit.

steps.title: Record 1D NOESY‑type 1H NMR spectrum
steps.instruction: Run the standard NOESY pulse sequence (noesygppr1d) with 256 scans, 65 536 data points, spectral width 8403.4 Hz, mixing time 10 ms, relaxation delay 5 s, and apply a 0.3 Hz line‑broadening; manually phase‑ and baseline‑correct using TopSpin 3.6.

steps.title: Process and quantify spectra with Chenomx
steps.instruction: Analyze the processed spectra in Chenomx NMR Suite 8.5 using the 600 MHz Version 11 database; identify metabolites by comparison with the database and literature, and quantify each by integrating the internal standard peak (TSP‑d₄).
